subject: Fraud & Scams
title: The Mark: Choosing a Victim
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Mark: Choosing a Victim usable.

hook.text: Con artists don't pick victims randomly. They profile for specific traits.

buildup.text: The ideal mark is trusting, slightly greedy, and too proud to admit being fooled.

discovery.text: Scammers test potential victims with small interactions to gauge how easily they trust.

twist.text: Intelligence doesn't protect you. In fact, smart people often make better marks — they're overconfident.

climax.text: The best marks are people who believe they're too clever to be conned.

punchline.text: The safest mark is the one who thinks they're immune.

quiz.question: Why are overconfident people good targets for cons?
options: They believe they can't be fooled
